content.title: About
content.content: Pink beans (varieties of Phaseolus vulgaris) are cooked beans with a light pink hue that develops during soaking and boiling. They have a soft, mildly sweet flesh, a gentle nutty aroma, and a pleasant texture. They are used in salads, side dishes, soups, and vegetarian meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The pink color appears after soaking and cooking, not in the raw bean.
Beans belong to the legume family and are a good source of plant protein.
In some cultures they are called “red” or “pink” beans, although they are not a separate cultivar.
Heat treatment destroys anti‑nutrients such as phytic acid, improving mineral absorption.
Pink beans are popular in Mexican and South American cuisines.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of cooked pink beans provides about 15 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and nerve‑muscle function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Cooked beans raise blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phytochemicals such as flavonoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Despite cooking, small amounts of phytic acid can reduce iron and zinc absorption.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans can cause bloating in sensitive people; introduce them gradually into the diet.

items.title: Sodium in processed products
items.content: Canned beans may contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add pink beans to salads, pastas, chili, soups, and stews. They work well in vegetarian patties or as a side dish for meat. For extra flavor, briefly sauté them with olive oil and your favorite spices before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pink beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze them in portioned bags – they keep well for up to 3 months. Discard any beans with off‑odors or signs of spoilage.
